🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin steadies above $81K as markets brace for the Fed, while Washington doubles down on stablecoins and Robinhood's crypto slump exposes cooling retail appetite. 📈 Bitcoin Reclaims $81K Ahead of Fed Decision Bitcoin climbed to around $81,400 after slipping below $80,000 on Tuesday, lifted by a rebound in Asian chip stocks as South Korea's Kospi jumped 6.6% and SK Hynix surged on a sevenfold profit jump. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in $176 million on Tuesday, a second straight day of inflows. CME FedWatch puts the odds of an unchanged rate at about 92%, with the decision due at 18:00 UTC and traders focused on Chair Kevin Warsh's guidance. Read full story 🇺🇸 Bessent: Crypto Will Fortify the U.S. Dollar Speaking at Ripple's Swell conference, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent framed digital assets as part of the U.S.-China technology race, saying America will "win in the digital asset stack." He argued dollar-backed stablecoins could become an important source of demand for Treasury debt, and said Treasury will work with the SEC and CFTC to fill the gap left by the failed Clarity Act and set guardrails against crypto debanking. More details ⚖️ CFTC Sues Utah to Shield Kalshi's Prediction Markets The Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed a federal challenge to block Utah's attorney general from stopping Kalshi's event contracts in the state, where gambling is constitutionally banned. Chairman Mike Selig argues federal authority preempts state law; the agency is now fighting 10 states in court as appellate rulings remain split on who regulates prediction markets. Read more 📉 Robinhood's Crypto Revenue Plunges 55% Robinhood's Q3 crypto transaction revenue fell to $120 million from about $267 million a year earlier, though it beat the $114.1 million consensus. Crypto trading volume dropped 38% to $50 billion, and crypto now makes up just 8.4% of total revenue of $1.42 billion. Prediction markets brought in $173 million, while overall EPS missed forecasts and shares slid about 5% after hours. See details 🤝 Robinhood Brings Ripple's RLUSD to Retail App Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin, now above $2.5 billion in market cap, will become available in the Robinhood app before the end of 2026, potentially reaching its 28.6 million funded customers. 81523.subject: Pearl’s Useful Work Test
81523.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Pearl’s pitch is Bitcoin without the waste. Bitcoin spends its security budget on hashes that are useless outside the chain, while Pearl’s miners do matrix multiplication that runs AI models, which in theory allows a GPU to earn an AI customer’s fee and a PEARL block reward at once.

Pearl runs cuPOW built on GPU matrix multiplication. Miners choose what to multiply, so the protocol proves only that the math was done, not that it served any AI requests, a dilemma at the core of the PEARL investment thesis.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3a20617f-e808-44e7-883e-4b09555a8285/image.png?t=1793164160)
Caption: 

Pearl is designed to be _**duplex mined **_(PEARL + AI work) on top of existing AI workloads at low overhead, but the network rewards the volume of multiplication and not what was multiplied. That favors _**synthetic miners**_ that only multiply random numbers for the sake of mining PEARL. A real AI server mines at a fraction of a dedicated miner’s speed, as most of its AI work is the wrong shape to count towards Pearl mining. 

**The upcoming **[FP8 hard fork](https://x.com/brezshares/status/2099927679223095738)** aims to switch mining to a standard format AI companies already use **on Nvidia’s Hopper and Blackwell data center chips. This would allow more recent open weight models like Llama and DeepSeek to be mineable without being rebuilt for Pearl, and would allow partial mineability of the latest generation of Mixture of Experts models. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4c3ff1ce-45c7-4d7f-83d8-f9efdae48d77/image.png?t=1793164160)
Caption: 

However, with few outside adopters and the upgrades not yet shipped, Pearl Research Labs is trying to make its own platform the best test of the thesis. On October 7, it was named one of six launch providers on [Liquid Inference](https://x.com/BrettHarrison/status/2107850779973304680), a new marketplace where providers compete on price for every request. This is the clearest case study for Pearl trying to make useful mining work in practice.

Controversially, Pearl Research Labs is also raising money to scale that test. On October 25, it [closed](https://x.com/doritsos/status/2114292001814294556) about $55M in equity and a $75M vehicle to build GPU capacity. I view this as a bullish sign for the thesis, since the lab, the team best placed to make the technology work, is now actively trying to prove it themselves and not waiting for outside providers.

There have been three key critiques in regards to the raise, but they are largely overblown in my view: 

1. _The lab sell
